cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, The Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Funds Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Funds Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Funds Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Funds Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Funds investment or in highly contested issues for which the Funds Adviser believes its vote is important to the Funds strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Advisers determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Funds best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Funds Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: Date of reporting period: July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024 A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Fund's Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Fund's Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Fund's Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Fund's Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Fund's investment or in highly contested issues for which the Fund's Adviser believes its vote is important to the Fund's strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Adviser's determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Fund's best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Fund's Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent, including for certain Funds that have strategies to invest in companies that the Fund's Adviser believes are sustainable leaders based on the Adviser's sustainability criteria or that meet certain other Environmental, Social, or Governance (ESG) criteria. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, The Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power over some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: During the reporting period, the MFS Conservative Allocation Portfolio, the MFS Growth Allocation Portfolio, and the MFS Moderate Allocation Portfolio, each a series of the Registrant (collectively, the "top tier funds") voted at the November 14, 2024 shareholder meetings of certain other investment companies registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, and sponsored by MFS (each, an "Underlying MFS Fund" and collectively, the "Underlying MFS Funds"). To address any potential conflicts of interest on the part of MFS that could arise from MFS voting shares of the MFS Underlying Funds on behalf of the top tier funds, MFS voted these Underlying MFS Fund shares in the same proportion as the other shareholders of the respective MFS Underlying Fund. Additionally, the top tier funds voted at the June 18, 2025 meeting of the MFS Growth Series, a series of MFS Variable Insurance Trust and MFS voted these shares in the same manner as described above (i.e., "mirror voting"). As a result, the voting record for these meetings will reflect a split vote. Columns 10 and 12 for an underlying fund reflect dollars of net asset value. Due to rounding the amounts in Column 12 may not total the amount in Column 10. Additionally, the amounts in columns 10 and 12 for the unanimous written consent of the shareholders of MFS Series Trust XIV-MFS Institutional Money Market Portfolio reflect dollars of net asset value.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. In addition, votes contained in this report include votes made by unaffiliated third-party investment advisors (External Advisors) who exercised voting power overs some or all of the securities voted. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing.The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: Date of reporting period: July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Fund's Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Fund's Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Fund's Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Fund's Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Fund's investment or in highly contested issues for which the Fund's Adviser believes its vote is important to the Fund's strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Adviser's determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Fund's best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Fund's Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent, including for certain Funds that have strategies to invest in companies that the Fund's Adviser believes are sustainable leaders based on the Adviser's sustainability criteria or that meet certain other Environmental, Social, or Governance (ESG) criteria. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

The Adviser has determined that, due to an inadvertent coding error, SOAUX had not properly set up its proxy voting procedures with its third-party proxy service providers. As a result, it appears that 16 proxies for SOAUX during the reporting period were not voted. The error has been corrected and the proper proxy voting process for SOAUX has been established. The Adviser and SOAUX will adhere to the proxy voting process to ensure that this issue is not repeated.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: A Fund does not have the right to vote proxies for securities on loans over a record date of such proxies. However, if a Funds Adviser has notice of the proxy in advance of the record date, the Funds Adviser may terminate a loan in advance of the record date if the Funds Adviser determines the vote is considered material with respect to an investment, such as when the Funds Adviser believes that its participation in the vote is necessary to preserve the long-term value of the Funds investment or in highly contested issues for which the Funds Adviser believes its vote is important to the Funds strategy. In determining whether a vote is material, the Advisers determination is informed by its responsibility to act in a Funds best interests. In most cases, the Adviser anticipates that the potential long-term value to a Fund of voting shares would not be material and would therefore not justify forgoing the potential revenue the loan may provide the Fund. This may result in proxies being voted by the borrower of the security in a way that would be contrary to how the Funds Adviser would vote if the security had not been lent, including for certain Funds that have strategies to invest in companies that the Funds Adviser believes are sustainable leaders based on the Advisers sustainability criteria or that meet certain other Environmental, Social, or Governance (ESG) criteria. However, in certain instances, the Adviser may determine, in its independent business judgment, that the value of voting outweighs the securities lending revenue loss to a Fund and may therefore recall shares to be voted in those instances.

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: The U.S. funds for which The Vanguard Group, Inc. (VGI) acts as investment advisor (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Board of Trustees for each of the Vanguard-advised funds has adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. Vanguard's Investment Stewardship Team administers the day-to-day operation of the funds' proxy voting process, overseen by the Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice pilots are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit about.vanguard.com/investment-stewardship.The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX by VGI were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, VGI's voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement

cover_fields.explanatoryNotes: On January 12, 2026, The Vanguard Group, Inc. ("VGI") and its affiliates (together, "Vanguard") completed an internal reorganization of portfolio management functions for the U.S. Vanguard funds into two wholly owned U.S. investment advisors, Vanguard Capital Management, LLC ("VCM") and Vanguard Portfolio Management, LLC ("VPM") (the "Internal Reorganization"). Each of these investment advisors consists of distinct investment management teams and investment stewardship teams with proxy voting administrative responsibilities. As of the effective date of the Internal Reorganization, VCM and VPM began exercising investment discretion and providing proxy voting administrative services for the funds to which they provide portfolio management services. The U.S. funds for which VGI acts as investment advisor through VCM and VPM (Vanguard-advised funds) retain authority to vote proxies received for the shares of equity securities held in each fund. To facilitate proxy voting for the Vanguard-advised funds, the Investment Committees of the Board of Trustees for the Vanguard-advised funds have adopted proxy voting procedures and policies to govern proxy voting for each portfolio retaining proxy voting authority. The Vanguard Capital Management Investment Stewardship Team and Vanguard Portfolio Management Investment Stewardship Team administer the day-to-day operations of the proxy voting process of the funds managed by VCM and VPM, respectively, as overseen by the relevant Investment Stewardship Oversight Committee appointed by each Investment Committee. In addition, a portion of the shares of certain funds participating in Vanguard's Investor Choice program are voted in accordance with policies selected by participating fund shareholders under Vanguard's Investor Choice program. For more information on the funds' proxy voting policies, please visit Proxy voting across Vanguard funds | Vanguard. The say-on-pay votes reported on this Form N-PX were calculated in accordance with the definition of "voting power" set forth under Rule 14Ad-1(d)(1) and 14Ad-1(d)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act). These include votes made on behalf of the Vanguard-advised funds and for which the Vanguard-advised funds retain authority to vote. Other rules, including those under Section 13 of the Exchange Act, utilize a definition of "voting power" that results in a divergent calculation methodology. Accordingly, the voting disclosures included in this filing may differ from information reported with respect to the voting power of VGI, VCM or VPM or the Vanguard-advised funds in other regulatory filings, including SEC filings made pursuant to Section 13. Votes made by VGI, VCM or VPM, or the External Advisors are identified in the proxy voting record according to their number assigned on the summary page of this filing. The votes reported do not reflect any votes cast pursuant to a regulatory requirement.
